decision: process-boundary orchestration fault campaign before real Qubes activation
winner: spawned coordinator process using the real durable OrchestratedMissionRuntime and MissionQueueStore

comparison.approach: spawned coordinator process + real durable DAG + kill/restart
comparison.correctness: high: exercises the actual orchestration graph, persisted queue, idempotent submission, worker ownership, restart recovery, and QA dependency join across an OS process boundary
comparison.robustness: high for the current single-store/single-live-coordinator design; covers committed-response loss and interrupted specialist recovery
comparison.latency: moderate test overhead from Node process startup, still suitable for CI
comparison.resourceUse: low: one short-lived child process at a time plus a temporary JSON store
comparison.regressionRisk: low: production queue/runtime semantics are unchanged; this adds a test harness and acceptance campaign
comparison.qa: asserts committed specialist attempts remain 1, interrupted specialist is reclaimed at attempt 2, stale old-session completion is rejected, idempotent resubmission creates no extra missions, QA stays blocked until recovery completes, and final graph is fully completed
cannot expose child lifecycle, stdio/process termination, or process-start recovery faults

comparison.approach: jump directly to real Qubes fault injection
comparison.robustness: environment-dependent until deterministic process behavior is proven
comparison.regressionRisk: high diagnostic ambiguity because VM policy/transport failures can mask orchestration-state failures
comparison.qa: still mandatory after this gate passes

whyItWon: It is the smallest step that materially crosses a real process boundary while still exercising the exact durable orchestration implementation. It separates queue/DAG restart correctness from Qubes policy and qrexec transport noise, giving failures a narrow diagnosis surface before VM-boundary testing.
failuresAndLessons: A process restart intentionally requeues work that was running but not durably completed; such work can execute again, so downstream side effects still require idempotency/fencing before real workers.
A completion persisted before response loss must remain completed after restart and must not be re-executed.
Session-scoped worker identities reject stale completions after restart, but a queue-level per-claim fencing token remains stronger for future multi-coordinator designs.
This test proves a single-live-coordinator process boundary, not simultaneous writers to one JSON snapshot and not a real Qubes/qrexec boundary.
nextGate: run the complete Node suite green on this head, then execute the same committed-response-loss and interrupted-specialist recovery invariants across an isolated qrexec worker/coordinator Qube boundary
